related_questions.question: What is the difference between aseptic meningitis and meningitis?
related_questions.snippet: Meningitis is an illness in which there is inflammation of the tissues that cover the brain and spinal cord. Viral or aseptic meningitis, which is the most common type, is caused by an infection with one of several types of viruses. Meningitis can also be caused by infections with several types of bacteria or fungi.

related_questions.question: What is the meaning of aseptic meningitis?
related_questions.snippet: Aseptic meningitis is a term used to describe inflammation of the meninges, the membranes covering the brain and spinal cord, caused by various factors and characterized by negative cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) bacterial cultures.

text_blocks.snippet: The ICD-10-CM code for aseptic meningitis due to AIDS is B20, followed by G03.0. First, code B20 (Human immunodeficiency virus [HIV] disease) is used to indicate the underlying HIV/AIDS condition. Then, code G03.0 (Nonpyogenic meningitis) is used to specify the aseptic meningitis manifestation.

list.snippet: B20: Human immunodeficiency virus [HIV] disease: This code signifies the presence of HIV infection and AIDS.
G03.0: Nonpyogenic meningitis: This code specifically denotes aseptic meningitis, which is often caused by viral infections, including those associated with HIV/AIDS.

list.title: Code First Note:
list.snippet: The ICD-10-CM guidelines require that the underlying condition (B20) be coded first, followed by the manifestation (G03.0).

list.title: Excludes1 Note:
list.snippet: There is an Excludes1 note under B20 that indicates if the meningitis is bacterial, it should not be coded with B20.
